title: Finite Cartier pole reduction agrees with site comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $r\geq1$, $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$, and a finite commutative $R$-algebra $\Lambda$. Let $Z$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible and $i:D\hookrightarrow Z$ an effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Write $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], use its exact derived inverse image, applied termwise [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] (on integral coefficients this is the exact inverse image of $\mathbf Z$-module sheaves of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$), and the ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$, take the Cartier pole extension $0	o\mathbf G_{m,\mathrm{et}}	o\mathcal M_D	o i_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathbf Z_D	o0$ (etale direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]), whose sections locally have the form $ut^{-a}$ for a regular equation $t$, and whose quotient sends $t^{-1}$ to $+1$. Its connecting morphism $ eta_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the last arrow of its short-exact-sequence triangle [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle], using the negative cone projection convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $B=
u_Z^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,\mathrm{et}}$, $G(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^	imes$, and let $a:B	o G$ be the units comparison adjoint to restriction on etale objects. Identify $
u_Z^{-1}i_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathbf Z_D$ with $F=i_{\mathrm{proet},*}\mathbf Z_D$ (pro-etale module direct image [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]) by the degree-zero adjunction-mate comparison of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], and set $ eta=a[1]
u_Z^{-1} eta_{\mathrm{et}}:F	o G[1]$.

For $L_R=-\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z_Z}R_Z$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], identify $L_R(F)$ with $i_*R_D$ by the quotient map and $L_R(G)$ with $\mu_{\ell^r,\mathrm{proet}}[1]$ by the Kummer normalization of [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction]: the scalar-extension unit becomes the Kummer connecting morphism. Under the roots comparison $
u_Z^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{\ell^r,\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf, lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections, lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and the supported-constant comparison, the entire morphism $L_R( eta)$ equals the comparison pullback of $L_R( eta_{\mathrm{et}})$. After derived extension to $\Lambda$, and the canonical supported-source and finite-Tate-line identifications, this morphism is precisely $c_D:i_*\Lambda_D	o\Lambda_Z(1)[2]$ of [sk-lem-geo-cartier]. These are the canonical adjunction-mate source and roots-induced target identifications, so the equality includes the supported restriction map and positive Kummer sign, not only the composite with $\Lambda_Z	o i_*\Lambda_D$.

proof.text: The etale supported coefficient generator is an unbounded derived unit. Its zero-shift Ext representative is therefore a CartierScalarUnit. The pro-etale integral residue sequence gives the residue unit directly on that site; normalized coefficient extension from the Cartier family and the supported generator identity give the full A-unit.

proof.text: For residue coefficients the root tensor maps are isomorphisms, so the positive Kummer connecting classes are the derived scalar units. Compose with normalized finite coefficient extension: the ordinary supported Kummer coefficient clause supplies the etale Tate unit, and the Cartier family supplies the pro-etale Tate unit. The tensor-generator equations identify the composed Ext classes with the exact Kummer representatives in the statement.

proof.text: Naturality of the positive Kummer Ext class under exact comparison and its kernel map gives the Kummer compatibility. Apply the exact scalar-boundary comparison square to transfer the entire etale pole-adjunct equation to the pro-etale one. This preserves the source mate and the supported restriction, without using faithfulness of scalar forgetting.

proof.text: For the simultaneous Cartier family, identify its etale boundary representative with the unique etale reduction, and then identify its comparison-normalized member with the unique pro-etale reduction. Substitute these equalities into its coefficient and Chern clauses. The same uniqueness proves the last characterization for every competing class. This retains the blueprint unit Cartier construction and its coefficient route.

tool_uses.why: Computes integral supported-constant stalks, needed for torsion-free source and quotient; the tower unit contains no general finite-stalk theorem.
Identifies constant integral stalks with Z, needed in the supported quotient calculation.
Turns the supported quotient stalk isomorphism into a sheaf isomorphism.
Provides exact inverse image for arbitrary discrete rings and the canonical qcqs direct-image comparisons, including units.
Identifies etale derived closed direct image with ordinary direct image for the degree-zero mate.
Provides the Grothendieck property of module sheaves on the chosen small pro-etale site.
Allows degree-zero direct-image identification on the pro-etale side.
Gives Kummer epimorphy on arbitrary schemes and on every pro-etale object; no finite-type restriction is available here.
Gives the canonical inverse-image section formula used to prove the roots-induced site isomorphism.
Gives roots pullback to every pro-etale scheme object, with its inclusion into units.
General normalized reduction naturality for maps of extensions and exact inverse images, exactly the homological-algebra tool needed here.
Supplies the actual module-valued derived scalar-extension functors for integral and finite coefficients.
Commutes exact site pullback with derived scalar extension by K-flat models.
Only its stated coefficient compatibility and canonical supported-source identification are used as a theorem; identification with its pole construction is proved from the source recipe.
Supplies finite etale roots-line flatness, so arbitrary finite coefficient extension has the specified degree-zero target.
Makes the degree-zero flat etale Tate-line complex K-flat.
Identifies local inverse-equation generators with the line-bundle torsor, for sign checking.
Identifies that torsor with its specified extension boundary, rather than an unnormalized H1 bijection.
